recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片中可見兩顆核有深折痕、凹陷的異型淋巴球：中央那顆中型細胞的核有明顯溝紋與折疊（大型 Sézary 細胞），右上那顆核呈不規則折疊；左側另有一顆小而深染的淋巴球作為大小對照。
features: Medium-sized lymphoid cell (center) with a deeply indented, grooved and folded nucleus and a thin rim of pale blue cytoplasm
Larger atypical lymphoid cell (upper right) with an irregularly folded nucleus, dense chromatin and pale cytoplasm with adherent granular material
Small mature-appearing lymphocyte with dense round nucleus at left for size comparison
Dense chromatin without conspicuous nucleoli in the atypical cells
Normochromic red cells with scattered platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows atypical lymphoid cells of varying size, including a medium-sized cell with a deeply grooved and folded nucleus and a thin rim of pale cytoplasm, and a larger cell with an irregularly convoluted nucleus. The chromatin is dense and nucleoli are not conspicuous. A small mature lymphocyte is present for comparison, and red cells and platelets are unremarkable. Findings are consistent with circulating Sezary cells, including large forms, in Sezary syndrome; flow cytometric confirmation is recommended.

ddx.vs: ATLL flower cells have multilobated petal-like nuclei with deep separations rather than fine cerebriform grooves, and occur with HTLV-1 infection.
Reactive lymphocytes have more abundant basophilic cytoplasm that indents around red cells and lack convoluted nuclear grooves.
Monocytes have folded nuclei but with lacy, less dense chromatin and abundant grey-blue vacuolated cytoplasm.
Mantle cell lymphoma cells can have cleaved nuclei but are CD5-positive B cells with cyclin D1 expression.
